title: new03, fts3 arm
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: fts3's segment writer binds zRoot SQLITE_STATIC into the cached segdir statement, steps and resets it, and sqlite3_reset() does not clear bindings, so parameter 6 still points at the buffer when fts3SegWriterFree() releases it. Fixed upstream in 3.23.0 (eab0e10304), sixteen days after 3.22.0 shipped
object: the fts3 segment writer's root buffer, still bound as parameter 6 of a persistent cached statement
lifetime_ender: fts3SegWriterFree() releases the buffer while the cached statement's binding still points at it
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Same upstream fix as case 21, kept as its own case because the two observables are independently reachable through different extensions. Corrected 2026-10-16: this said case 22, which is fix-2026-07-26 and unrelated; the pair sharing eab0e10304 is 21 (rtree) and 23 (fts3), and the renumber from 38 cases to 33 on 2026-10-06 left both halves pointing at the wrong row. Of the two, this is the better-made one: its corpus case.c and the CheriBSD arm's copy were already byte-identical, where case 21's had diverged, and its consequence is visible on every arm without the trigger having to reclaim the freed block

status: re-measured on all four readings 2026-10-16 on this platform and every verdict holds. host ASan is the 2026-10-11 bundle's reading: READ of size 1492, 0 bytes into a freed 4064-byte region, sqlite3VdbeSerialPut <- sqlite3VdbeExec <- sqlite3_step, freed by fts3SegWriterFree <- fts3SegmentMerge <- fts3DoOptimize, allocated by fts3SegWriterAdd <- fts3SegmentMerge; not re-run, this host has no x86 ASan runtime. virtual-malloc MISSED, RETURNED, both controls as declared. virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=25 pc=0x3fb18020f8 offset 204 in memcpy, both controls as declared; it faults at the stale read and never reaches the VERDICT line. cheribsd-revocation MISSED, RETURNED rc=0, with the boot's positive control trapping and revocation knobs 1/0. Every run reaches the defect and rewrites the %_segdir row: before len=1665 sum=3435050182 first4=483692, then sum_changed=1 first4_changed=1 at the same length. The bytes that land in the row differ by platform and are recorded in the note. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16; every verdict holds and no count moves. Three records are corrected and one new reading is worth keeping. (1) fidelity pointed at the wrong sibling; see there. (2) The attribution is no longer 'any memcpy would count'. Probe site 58 hooks the SQLITE_STATIC bind in fts3WriteSegdir, the free of pWriter->aData in fts3SegWriterFree, and the copy in sqlite3VdbeSerialPut, the last filtered to len>400 so the 1665-byte root buffer separates from that hot function's ordinary traffic. On CheriBSD purecap the three print one pointer value: SERIAL z=0x218200 len=1665 first4=0x7616c on the legitimate write, FREE aData=0x218200 nData=1665, then after the re-step marker SERIAL z=0x218200 len=1665 first4=0x40050000 -- same pointer, changed content. So the memcpy Sublet faults in is the one copying out of the freed root buffer. (3) The physical sublet row reports cause 24, which cannot distinguish a revoked capability from one that never was, so the Sublet cell rests on the virtual arm's cause 25; it is marked in results/matrix.tsv. The new reading: this is the one case so far where the ADDRESS judgement is correct and sufficient. The block is not reissued before the read, so site 58 reports kind=UAF off=0 n=1665 req=4061 blk=0x218200, with req=4061 matching the 4064-byte region host ASan reports and the 1665-byte read sitting inside it -- not the kind=OOB misclassification cases 12, 21 and 22 produced when a reclaimed block made the read exceed the new request. It also shows why this case produces no false positive on the two non-Sublet arms, unlike 19, 20 and 22: tag=1 and cb=<arena>+262144 at the read, so there is nothing for either architecture to object to, and what is read is BYTES rather than a pointer, so no forged pointer is ever dereferenced. The consequence is still plainly visible without any mechanism, and the bytes differ by platform, all of them read out of the same dead buffer: first4 becomes 0xFFFFFFFF on base Capstone, which is memsys5's own Mem5Link next=-1 terminator; 0x40050000 on CheriBSD; and 0x60ed69d4 on the host, which the case header notes looks like a heap pointer. PRAGMA integrity_check disagrees by platform too and is not a reliable signal here: SQLITE_CORRUPT on CheriBSD and on the host, but SQLITE_NOMEM on base Capstone, where the 256 KiB arena cannot complete the check. The signal to report is the changed row, not integrity_check
fault_sites_why: The cached segdir statement's parameter 6 still points at the buffer fts3SegWriterFree released; stepping it copies the binding in sqlite3VdbeSerialPut (consumer), with memcpy. Weaker than a single function: any memcpy under it would count. Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual runs resolved faults there; the reason is the source and PROVENANCE.md cited, which predate those runs. STRENGTHENED 2026-10-16 by probe site 58, which replaces the function-level claim with pointer identity: the pointer fts3WriteSegdir binds SQLITE_STATIC as parameter 6, the pointer fts3SegWriterFree releases, and the pointer sqlite3VdbeSerialPut copies out of are printed at all three hooks and are one value. The length agrees as well -- len=1665 at the copy is nData at the free -- and on this case the address judgement independently confirms it, kind=UAF off=0 n=1665 req=4061 on the same block.
